claims.claim: a wind-mortality term on the embryos explained 52–61 % of the year-to-year variation in perch egg masses in four of six demes at Lochaber Lake, Nova Scotia (Aalto & Newsome 1993, abstract)
claims.note: full text not obtained. Even the abstract, which the paper says it relies on, reads differently: the models that explain '52–61%' of the variation in four of six demes use 'lagged egg-mass counts and winds' together (a model with an instantaneous wind mortality rate on the embryonic stage), so the 52–61 % belongs to the whole model, not to the wind term alone. The abstract does not name the lake ('our study lake'); Lochaber Lake, Nova Scotia comes from the authors' earlier papers (per the research note). Suggested wording until the article is read: 'models combining the previous egg-mass count with wind-driven embryo mortality explained 52–61 % of the year-to-year variation in egg-mass counts in four of six demes'
